# Starter principles: Product

- Skill: `product-principles`
- Offered when: people use what the project makes.

## Lines

- A person gets what they came for in as few steps as possible, receives it before being asked for anything, and is stopped at a gate only where a step truly requires one — every extra step costs some people, and a gate ahead of the answer settles nothing. Yields for a gate that protects — sign-in where work is kept, consent, an abuse limit, confirming an act that cannot be undone — and for a step the person needs in order to choose or to trust what follows.
- A feature, setting or step is added only once a real need for it has appeared, and fewer things ship complete rather than more ship half-done — every addition is met by each person and has to be kept true by the project. Yields when the absent piece stops the main task from working.
- What every person gets without setting anything up works, can be changed where they already work, and follows what the product can observe instead of asking — someone unaware that a setting exists is stuck with its default all the same. Yields when one default cannot serve a known group of people; then the chosen default is stated, with its reason.
- Before a press that uses up something, makes the person wait long or can never be reversed, the control states what will be consumed and what comes back, and no default spends anything unannounced — a cost found out after the press feels like a trick. Yields when the cost is too small for anyone to weigh.
- A person hears that something is finished, measured or included only when it truly is, and a gap is named rather than papered over, on every surface, document and message the project produces — once someone catches one untrue claim, they doubt all the rest. Holds without a yield.
- Where a person sits waiting on a step, a slower step has to justify its time; where nobody waits, the time goes to quality or cost — the person pays each wait on every use. Yields when the slower step stops a harmful result from reaching the person.
- A result appears as soon as it is whole and correct, and no wait is shortened by thinning out what the person is told — a fast wrong answer costs more trust than the time it saved. Yields where the person asked for an early partial result and it is labelled as partial.
- Only where the project collects usage analytics: When a flow is built or changed, the same change records when it begins, each stage, when it completes, and every failure or drop-out — without that record, guesses take the place of what people actually went through. Yields when an event would gather data beyond what the privacy terms already allow.
- Choice — what a product call rests on. Default side, unless what ships reaches people the project cannot easily reach again, or cannot be quietly withdrawn; then the other side.
  - Default side: A product call rests on something people were seen to do — pick, switch, work around, or leave alone — which the change names, and when a direction is good enough it ships and actual use steers the following round — a made-up story or one anecdote cannot show what people want, and live use is the least costly evidence available. Yields while nobody uses the product yet; then the call is named as a bet.
  - Other side: A product call rests on research done before building — interviews, tests with a prototype — since learning by shipping costs too much where a change is public or hard to withdraw. Yields for a change that can be withdrawn without anyone noticing.
- Work a person made or earned is never taken away by a refresh, a release, a cancellation or a change of method — losing work they did nothing to lose is where a product does the most harm to the people it serves. Yields to the person's own deliberate act, once its outcome has been stated, and to retention rules that demand deletion, applied with warning and a chance to export first.
- Only where use of the product costs money: Every per-use cost ships with a hard cap and an off switch, placed where sensible use never reaches it, and a person stopped by the cap has their work queued or is told when it will continue — a single loop gone wrong or a single bad actor must not set the bill. Holds without a yield; the cap moves only by the owner's decision.
- A behavior people rely on changes only with notice they can see before the change lands — a silent change breaks what people built on the old behavior. Yields for removing a behavior that was itself harming people; then the notice follows the fix.
- Each feature names, before it is built, the observable result that will show it worked and where to read it — without that, a feature that shipped cannot be told from one that works. Yields for a fix restoring a behavior that already had one.
